title: Fieldwork
caption: A storefront, connected analytics, and reproducible experiments.
narration: Welcome to Fieldwork. This demo follows a shopping journey into product analytics, web analytics, and experimentation. The application uses live Supabase and PostHog connections. All shoppers and payments are fictional.

title: Start with a real shopping flow
caption: Working product interactions, not a static mockup.
narration: Fieldwork Supply is the customer facing store. Shoppers can explore products, choose a fictional account, build a bag, and complete a simulated purchase.

title: Control A: explore, then add
caption: The original product card opens details before adding to the bag.
narration: The experiment starts with the original product cards. In control A, shoppers open a product detail dialog before adding an item. Preview visits are excluded from analytics.

title: Treatment B: add from the card
caption: A direct Add to bag button removes the product-detail step.
narration: Treatment B puts Add to bag directly on the product card and makes the demo sign in requirement visible. This is the change the experiment measures.

title: A stable visitor, a fictional account
caption: Assignments persist in Supabase and survive demo sign-in.
narration: Now we leave preview mode and select a fictional shopper. The visitor's experiment assignment is persisted before the cards render, and choosing an account does not change that assignment.

title: Complete a demo purchase
caption: Database prices, a saved order, and no real payment.
narration: Add a bottle, begin checkout, and select the demo payment method. Placing the order saves the order and its items in Supabase. No real payment is taken.

title: Check the less obvious journeys
caption: Return from checkout, remove an item, and switch demo accounts.
narration: A useful demo includes edge cases. Return from checkout to the bag, remove an item, and switch fictional accounts. These journeys exercise the application, rather than simply generating a chart.

title: From shopping activity to product analytics
caption: Persisted orders power the dashboard and product revenue tables.
narration: The separate analytics workspace reads persisted orders. It shows shoppers, purchases, revenue, and checkout progression, while keeping the source and date window visible.

title: Inspect the experiment
caption: Two thousand fictional visitors. A planted effect, clearly labeled.
narration: The synthetic experiment contains two thousand fictional visitors. Its treatment effect is deliberately planted. The results are queried from stored events, and they do not establish real business lift.

title: Reproduce the result in either source
caption: Switch Supabase to PostHog and inspect the comparison and query time.
narration: Switch the query source from Supabase to PostHog. The app independently compares conversion, revenue, event counts, and the displayed segments. Matching totals are shown alongside the query timestamp.

title: Explore the journey behind the headline
caption: Product funnels, web engagement, device and acquisition-channel segments.
narration: Go beyond the headline conversion rate. Inspect product engagement, cart additions, checkout progression, and payment errors. Device and acquisition channel breakdowns help identify where to investigate next.

title: Keep the evidence attached
caption: Inspect queries, returned aggregates, and separate live demo traffic.
narration: The method view exposes the source queries and returned aggregates. A separate live demo cohort captures actual store interactions with fictional shoppers. Sparse samples are shown without an unsupported confidence interval.

title: From behavior to evidence
caption: Fieldwork Supply + Fieldwork Analytics
narration: That is the product workflow: a working store, persistent transactions, independently queryable analytics, and an experiment whose provenance stays attached to the result.

title: Now ask the analyst
caption: Real OpenAI responses, read-only tools, and inspectable evidence.
narration: Now we add the AI analyst. These are actual OpenAI responses generated during the recording. The agent can select approved read only tools, but it cannot change orders or execute arbitrary SQL.

title: Question 1: can we ship variant B?
caption: Ask about the result, the guardrails, and the limits of synthetic evidence.
narration: Ask whether the quick add experiment supports shipping the change. Fieldwork must retrieve evidence and distinguish a planted synthetic effect from a production recommendation.

title: An explanation grounded in tools
caption: Read the actual answer and inspect its evidence.
narration: The model explains the evidence returned by its tools. It should identify the synthetic dataset and its limitations. The numbers are computed by the data sources, rather than invented in the answer.

title: Question 2: which products earn revenue?
caption: Move from the synthetic experiment to live demo commerce.
narration: Next, ask which products generate the most revenue in the live demo store. This question uses the application order data, separately from the scripted experiment fixture.

title: Follow the answer back to the database
caption: Open the product tool's returned rows and exact RPC.
narration: Each answer carries evidence chips. Open a chip to inspect the product rows, the selected dataset, the date window, and the exact database query behind the explanation.

title: Question 3: do the systems agree?
caption: Compare Supabase orders with canonical PostHog order events.
narration: Finally, ask whether database orders match PostHog. This demonstrates investigation across systems, rather than simply summarizing a single dashboard.

title: Surface agreement and discrepancies
caption: Inspect the actual reconciliation result and its stated scope.
narration: Inspect the returned reconciliation evidence. If events are missing or delivery is still pending, the discrepancy should remain visible. Capture acceptance alone does not prove an event is stored.

title: An analyst you can inspect
caption: Ask a question. Query the sources. Review the evidence.
narration: Fieldwork connects a working product to an analyst with inspectable evidence. The strongest demonstration is the full loop: collect activity, query independent sources, ask a useful question, and verify the answer.
